sections.title: C-1: Equipment
sections.summary: Joint sawing checklist items covering the sawing equipment itself: number of saws, use of early-age entry saws, and saw blade type compatibility with the concrete's aggregate type.
sections.body: The equipment checklist for joint sawing operations covers: the number of saws available for the operation; the use of early-age entry saws (which can begin cutting sooner after placement than conventional saws); and confirming that the saw blade type is compatible with the concrete's aggregate type, since blade selection affects both cut quality and the potential for raveling.
key_points: Confirm the number of saws available for the sawing operation.
Confirm availability and use of early-age entry saws.
Confirm saw blade type is compatible with the concrete aggregate type.
sections.applicability: Applies to verifying sawing equipment readiness and suitability before and during joint sawing operations.

sections.title: C-2: Inspection Items
sections.summary: Joint sawing checklist items for field inspection: test strip sawing, comparing planned versus actual sawcut locations, acceptable raveling/spalling limits, sawcut depth (initial and reservoir), timing of longitudinal joint sawing, ensuring the sawcut is carried through the vertical edge, handling of odd-shaped slabs at radii, and high tie bar situations.
sections.body: The inspection items to be checked during joint sawing include: performing test strip sawing before full production sawing; comparing planned versus actual sawcut locations; confirming that raveling and spalling along the sawcut remain within acceptable limits; verifying sawcut depth for both the initial cut and the sealant reservoir cut; confirming the timing of longitudinal joint sawing; confirming the sawcut is carried through the vertical edge of the slab; checking treatment of odd-shaped slabs at radii, where standard sawing patterns may not apply directly; and checking high tie bar situations, where a tie bar positioned too near the surface could be struck by the saw blade.
key_points: Perform test strip sawing before production sawing.
Compare planned versus actual sawcut locations.
Confirm raveling and spalling remain within acceptable limits.
Verify sawcut depth for both the initial cut and the reservoir cut.
Confirm timing of longitudinal joint sawing.
Confirm the sawcut is carried through the vertical edge.
Check treatment of odd-shaped slabs at radii.
Check for high tie bar situations that risk the saw blade striking the bar.
sections.applicability: Applies to field inspection during active joint sawing operations on a concrete pavement project.

sections.title: C-3: Cold Weather, Rain, and Slow Concrete Setting Times
sections.summary: Joint sawing checklist items for conditions that delay concrete setting: use of insulation or geotextile fabric, checking fly ash usage requirements, considering early-age entry sawing, and considering skip sawing.
sections.body: When cold weather, rain, or otherwise slow concrete setting times are encountered, the following items should be checked: the use of insulation or geotextile fabric to help maintain curing temperature; fly ash usage requirements, since fly ash content affects the rate of strength gain and therefore the timing of sawing; consideration of early-age entry sawing to compensate for a delayed set; and consideration of skip sawing (cutting alternate joints first) to keep pace with a slower or interrupted setting schedule.
key_points: Consider use of insulation or geotextile fabric during cold weather or slow-setting conditions.
Check fly ash usage requirements, which affect strength gain rate and sawing timing.
Consider early-age entry sawing to compensate for delayed set.
Consider skip sawing to keep pace with slower or interrupted setting.
sections.applicability: Applies when cold weather, rain, or slow concrete setting times complicate the timing of joint sawing operations.

sections.title: C-4: Post-Cutting Issues
sections.summary: Joint sawing checklist items for post-cutting activities: flushing joints, re-application of curing compound, timing of backer rod placement, and early-age cracking inspection.
sections.body: After joint sawcutting is complete, the following post-cutting items should be checked: flushing joints to remove sawing slurry and residue; re-application of curing compound where the original application was disturbed by the sawing operation; timing of backer rod placement in the sawed joint reservoir; and inspection for early-age cracking that may have developed during or after the sawing operation.
key_points: Flush joints to remove sawing slurry and residue.
Re-apply curing compound where disturbed by sawing.
Confirm timing of backer rod placement in the joint reservoir.
Inspect for early-age cracking following the sawing operation.
sections.applicability: Applies to the checks performed immediately after joint sawcutting is complete on a concrete pavement project.
